name: SPlisHSPlasH + splashsurf
role: SPH fluid simulator paired with splashsurf CLI/library for particle-to-mesh surface reconstruction
notes: 2026-11-15: Assess because the digest describes a bakeable particle simulation and mesh-sequence workflow beyond rigid-body solvers. Revisit after confirming build and Python/CLI support on target machines and cross-machine reproducibility.

2026-11-15: Assessment uncertainty: release recency and reproducible SPlisHSPlasH build/export steps on target machines were not established; assess the GPL simulator and MIT reconstruction component separately.
2026-11-24: Toolkit guide written from partial evidence (headless 2D dam break; reruns not bit-identical at default threads, reproducible only with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 as a diagnostic).

evidence.result: Partial: 9 of 11 predeclared checks pass. Headless 2D DFSPH dam break, 266 particles, fixed 0.002 s step, 500 steps via pySPlisHSPlasH 2.19.1 on Python 3.12.13 and numpy 2.5.5: count conserved at 5 frames, all particles inside the box, centre of mass drops 0.157 m and width grows 1.40 m, 2D positions. reruns_identical and seek_fresh_process_matches_trace fail at default threads: particles differ by 0.30 m at step 500 between reruns. Diagnostic only: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 gives bit-identical reruns and seeks. No expected/ kept.
evidence.scope: Fixture-reported: headless 2D dam break, Python bindings only; count, box bounds, fall and spread pass; reruns and fresh-process seeks not bit-identical at default threads; no splashsurf.

summary: SPlisHSPlasH simulates particle based fluids; the companion splashsurf project reconstructs SPH particle data as surface meshes, with Rust CLI/library and Python bindings. Together they support a scriptable simulation-to-mesh workflow, while simulation build and export settings remain environment dependent.
use_when: Bake particle fluid simulations and reconstruct a mesh sequence
Choose SPH particle workflows over rigid-body solvers
Use splashsurf to turn SPlisHSPlasH particle output into surface meshes
avoid_when: Use a rigid-body solver for primarily solid-object dynamics
Use Blender fluid tools when an integrated scene authoring workflow matters more

install.macos: SPlisHSPlasH Python bindings: in a Python 3.12 venv, `pip install --only-binary=:all: pySPlisHSPlasH==2.19.1` (PyPI macOS arm64 wheel, no CLI, no source build needed); splashsurf: `cargo install splashsurf` or `pip install pysplashsurf` (not exercised by any example)

assessment.version_seen: Current source repositories; release versions/dates not confirmed
assessment.last_release: unknown (release dates not established from pages read)
assessment.rationale: Official repositories document the simulator and separate splashsurf CLI/library/Python surface reconstruction route. Both projects state MIT; the official org page lists SPlisHSPlasH updated 2026-10-28, while release dates and reproducible target-machine builds remain unverified.
